name: Nicaragua
summary: Independent in 1838; ruled by the Somoza family (1936–79), overthrown by the Sandinista revolution; a war with US-backed Contras followed.

terrain.value: Pacific lowlands with Central America’s two largest lakes and volcanoes, central highlands, and the Caribbean lowlands of the Mosquito Coast.

climate.value: Tropical, with a wet season from May to October, hurricanes on the Caribbean coast, and a drier Pacific side.

resources.value: Coffee, beef, gold, sugar, fertile volcanic soils and fish.

population.value: About 6.5 million people in the early 2020s (estimates vary).

urbanisation.value: Managua, the capital, holds about a quarter of the people; León and Granada are the old colonial cities.

disease.value: Dengue and malaria are the main mosquito-borne diseases, and storms and floods raise the risk of outbreaks.

migration.value: Many have emigrated to Costa Rica and the United States, especially since the 1980s war and later unrest.

economicBase.value: Farming (coffee, beef, sugar), gold mining, textiles in free-trade zones and money sent home by emigrants.

tradeRoutes.value: Exports go by road and port, mostly to the United States and Central America; the Pacific and Caribbean ports are small.

wealth.value: A lower-middle-income country; one of the poorest in the Americas.

moneyAndTax.value: The córdoba, named after Francisco Hernández de Córdoba, the Spanish explorer.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

keyRulers.value: Anastasio Somoza García. Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: The Sandinistas deposed Somoza in 1979; Violeta Chamorro’s coalition won the 1990 election.

institutions.value: Independent courts, elections and the press have been weakened since 2007.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: The National Guard under the Somoza family was replaced by the Sandinista army after 1979; today a small army and police.

territoryChange.value: Nicaragua’s borders have stayed much the same since independence, apart from the Mosquito Coast, which joined in 1860 and 1894.

alliancesRivals.value: Opposed the United States during the Contra war (1980s); now closer to Russia and China.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: The Literacy Crusade of 1980 cut illiteracy sharply, according to government and UNESCO figures.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Roads and the Pan-American Highway; the east coast has few roads and relies on rivers and boats.

religion.value: Mostly Catholic, with a large and growing Protestant (Evangelical) minority.

artsArchitecture.value: Poetry is central, led by Rubén Darío (died 1916), and colonial architecture in León and Granada.

socialStructure.value: A mestizo majority, with Indigenous and Afro-descendant communities on the Caribbean coast.

sharedIdentity.value: A strong national identity tied to poetry, the 1979 revolution, and resistance to outside interference.

dailyLife.value: Many families live in simple homes in towns or farming villages; gallo pinto (rice and beans) is a daily meal.

ideasReligions.value: Liberation theology, which linked Catholic faith with social justice, was influential in the 1970s–80s.

colonisation.value: Part of the Spanish Empire until 1821.

riseSignals.value: Independence from Spain (1821) and from the Central American Federation (1838).

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Nicaragua continues as an independent republic.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
